These chips are a real power envelope, not a label. Every percentage is taken from the capability the device advertises (the highest step its driver states), never from the ceiling the system happens to allow right now. So gaming and performance never sit below an untouched device: when the device\'s own policy holds a lower ceiling they ask for the advertised one, and the log writes what it was, what the device can do and what was requested. Below that, the share caps the GPU ceiling and every CPU policy you did not set by hand, rounded down to a real frequency step, and a cooling preset (balanced, power, custom) only ever lowers a ceiling — it never raises one. On top of that, a thermal guard lowers the same ceilings while the device is throttling and restores them when it cools, never above what you chose.
